title: Self-supervised Topic Taxonomy Discovery in the Box Embedding Space
venue: Transactions of the Association for Computational Linguistics, 12, 1401-1416
problem: Point and hyperbolic embeddings in hierarchical neural topic models use symmetric distances, so they cannot express the asymmetric parent-child relation between topics, and randomly initialised upper-level topics can collapse.
architecture: BoxTM: VAE with logistic-normal prior encodes TF-IDF documents; words and topics are hyperrectangles (box embeddings) whose volume reflects semantic scope; topic-word distributions come from symmetric box affinities and hierarchy from an asymmetric box metric; upper-level topics are learned bottom-up by recursive Affinity Propagation clustering on topic boxes; two self-supervised tasks model the semantic scopes of words and topics.
key_results: 20news: C 0.301 vs HyperMiner 0.224, C*D 0.199 vs TaxoGen 0.159, HC 0.159 vs nTSNTM 0.134.
NYT: C 0.409, C*D 0.265, HC 0.177 (best); TaxoGen reaches higher diversity D (0.881 vs 0.648).
arXiv: C 0.257, C*D 0.173, HC 0.113 (best); TaxoGen D 0.681 vs BoxTM 0.672.

strengths.text: Box volumes give an explicit, asymmetric notion of topic generality, and clustering-based initialisation of upper levels alleviates topic collapse.
Learns a deep taxonomy on the large arXiv corpus where SawETM and HyperMiner fail to learn a deep taxonomy.

limitations.text: Topic diversity is lower than the clustering-based TaxoGen on all three datasets.
Box embeddings make training more costly than point embeddings; the authors list more efficient box computation as future work.

notes: Queue listed this as arXiv; Crossref confirms the TACL version (DOI 10.1162/tacl_a_00712), which is the version to cite.
